vulnerable_architecture: A Node.js/Express reporting endpoint builds a raw SQL query by string-concatenating a 'sort' query parameter into an ORDER BY clause, with no allowlist of valid column names.
theoretical_attack_kill_chain: Attacker sends baseline request with sort=name to confirm normal ordering behavior
Attacker injects sort=(SELECT 1) to test for raw query evaluation
Attacker determines column count via sort=1 UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,NULL--
Attacker extracts schema metadata using placeholder payload: sort=1 UNION SELECT table_name,NULL,NULL FROM information_schema.tables--
Attacker pivots to extracting non-sensitive placeholder values from a target table for demonstration purposes only
synthetic_server_logs: [app-log] ERROR: SequelizeDatabaseError: syntax error at ReportService.js:112 — unexpected token NULL
detection_logic_for_ai: Flag query parameters containing SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, information_schema) in non-SQL-intended fields like 'sort'; alert on abrupt response-size changes following parameter mutation; correlate repeated ORDER BY injections with database error log spikes from the same source IP.
secure_code_remediation: const ALLOWED_SORT_COLUMNS = ['name','date','id']; const sortCol = ALLOWED_SORT_COLUMNS.includes(req.query.sort) ? req.query.sort : 'name'; db.query('SELECT * FROM reports ORDER BY ??', [sortCol]);

vulnerability_cve_category: Server-Side Request Forgery via Webhook Validator (CWE-918)
vulnerable_architecture: A SaaS platform lets users register a webhook URL and 'test' it server-side; the test function fetches the URL directly without restricting destination IP ranges or schemes.
theoretical_attack_kill_chain: Attacker registers a webhook pointing to an external test endpoint to confirm server-side fetch behavior
Attacker changes the webhook URL to a cloud metadata endpoint placeholder: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/
Attacker tries alternate schemes (file://, gopher://) to test filter bypass resilience
Attacker uses a DNS-rebinding placeholder domain that resolves externally first, then to an internal IP, to bypass naive first-request allowlisting
synthetic_server_logs: [app-log] WARN: Outbound fetch to link-local address 169.254.169.254 blocked by egress policy — source: webhook-tester-svc
detection_logic_for_ai: Monitor outbound requests initiated by server-side fetch utilities for destinations in RFC1918, loopback, and link-local ranges; flag non-HTTP(S) schemes (file://, gopher://, dict://) in user-supplied URLs; alert on repeated webhook URL changes within short time windows from a single account.

vulnerable_architecture: A background job queue stores serialized Python objects (via pickle) in a Redis-backed cache, and worker processes deserialize the data on retrieval without integrity verification (no HMAC signing).
theoretical_attack_kill_chain: Attacker identifies that cached job payloads are base64-encoded pickle streams by inspecting response headers/cookies
Attacker confirms deserialization occurs server-side by submitting a malformed pickle stream and observing an UnpicklingError in logs
Attacker crafts a placeholder object referencing a benign __reduce__ method (e.g., returning a harmless tuple) purely to demonstrate code-path triggering, without any real payload
Attacker submits the crafted object as a job payload to confirm execution during deserialization
synthetic_server_logs: [worker-log] ERROR: pickle.UnpicklingError: could not find module 'bad_module' at JobWorker.py:67
[worker-log] WARN: Deserialized object triggered __reduce__ invocation — class reference: builtins.eval (flagged as suspicious pattern)
detection_logic_for_ai: Flag any pickle stream containing references to builtins.eval, os.system, subprocess, or other code-execution primitives in __reduce__ metadata; alert on UnpicklingError spikes; treat any use of raw pickle.loads() on data crossing a trust boundary as a high-severity architectural finding regardless of payload content.
secure_code_remediation:
import json
# Replace pickle with a safe, schema-validated format
job_data = json.loads(payload)
validate_schema(job_data, JOB_SCHEMA)
# Never call pickle.loads() on untrusted or network-sourced data

vulnerable_architecture: A billing API exposes invoice details at /api/invoices/{id} using a sequential integer primary key, and the authorization check only verifies that the requester is logged in, not that they own the specific invoice.
theoretical_attack_kill_chain: Attacker logs in as a legitimate low-privilege user and retrieves their own invoice at /api/invoices/4471
Attacker increments the ID to /api/invoices/4472 and observes a 200 OK response containing another customer's placeholder invoice data
Attacker scripts sequential enumeration across a range of IDs to confirm the pattern is systemic
Attacker notes which responses return 200 vs 403 to map the accessible ID space
synthetic_server_logs: [app-log] INFO: 40 sequential invoice requests from single session token within 12 seconds — no ownership validation performed
detection_logic_for_ai: Detect sequential or near-sequential resource ID access patterns from a single authenticated session in a short time window; cross-reference requested resource owner ID against authenticated user ID at the log level; flag high-velocity enumeration (>N requests/minute to a parameterized ID endpoint).

vulnerability_cve_category: Remote Code Execution via Unrestricted File Upload (CWE-434)
vulnerable_architecture: A profile-picture upload feature on a PHP application validates file type only via client-supplied MIME-type header and file extension string matching, storing uploads directly in a web-accessible directory with execute permissions.
theoretical_attack_kill_chain: Attacker uploads a benign .jpg to confirm the upload pipeline and storage path
Attacker renames a placeholder test script to profile.php.jpg to probe double-extension handling
Attacker uploads a file with a spoofed Content-Type: image/jpeg header while the body contains non-image placeholder text, to test MIME validation depth
Attacker requests the uploaded file path directly to check whether the server executes it based on the true extension
synthetic_server_logs: [app-log] ERROR: PHP Parse error in /uploads/test.php.jpg on line 1 — unexpected token (file executed by handler)
[app-log] WARN: Upload directory /uploads/ served with execute permissions — flagged by config auditor
detection_logic_for_ai: Flag uploads where the filename contains multiple extensions or a server-executable extension (.php, .jsp, .asp) regardless of declared Content-Type; alert on any subsequent GET request to an uploaded file path that returns a server-side error indicating interpretation rather than static serving; verify magic-byte file signature matches declared type.

vulnerable_architecture: A Java-based invoice-import feature parses user-uploaded XML files using a DocumentBuilderFactory with external entity resolution enabled by default.
theoretical_attack_kill_chain: Attacker uploads a well-formed XML invoice to confirm the parser accepts and processes files
Attacker submits an XML file declaring a placeholder external entity pointing to a local, non-sensitive test file to confirm entity expansion occurs
Attacker observes the parsed output reflects file content, confirming XXE
Attacker tests a placeholder SSRF-style entity referencing an internal test URL to assess blended XXE/SSRF impact
synthetic_server_logs: 192.0.2.88 - - [04/Oct/2026:08:12:30 +0000] "POST /api/invoices/import HTTP/1.1" 200 982 "-" "Mozilla/5.0" Content-Type: application/xml body=<!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///tmp/test_placeholder.txt">]><invoice>&xxe;</invoice>
[app-log] WARN: XML parser resolved external entity reference to local filesystem path /tmp/test_placeholder.txt
[app-log] ERROR: Unexpected content in invoice field 'description' — matches local file content pattern
detection_logic_for_ai: Scan inbound XML payloads for DOCTYPE declarations containing ENTITY and SYSTEM/PUBLIC keywords; flag any XML parse operation that results in file-path-like or URL-like content being reflected in application output; alert on parser configuration lacking FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING or external entity disabling.

vulnerable_architecture: A Flask application renders user-supplied 'nickname' input directly into a Jinja2 template string via render_template_string() instead of passing it as a safe context variable.
theoretical_attack_kill_chain: Attacker submits a nickname containing a benign template expression placeholder: {{7*7}}
Attacker observes the rendered page displays 49, confirming server-side template evaluation
Attacker probes object traversal depth with a placeholder expression: {{ self.__class__.__init__.__globals__ }}
Attacker notes which globals/builtins are exposed to assess theoretical blast radius, without constructing a working RCE payload
synthetic_server_logs: [app-log] WARN: Jinja2 template rendered user input directly via render_template_string — introspection expression detected
detection_logic_for_ai: Flag user input fields containing template delimiter patterns ({{ }}, {% %}, ${ }) regardless of target language; alert when rendered output contains evaluated arithmetic or object-introspection artifacts (e.g., a numeric result where text was expected, or class/module names); treat any use of render_template_string() on user-controlled strings as a high-risk code pattern during static analysis.

vulnerable_architecture: An API verifies JWTs by calling a verification library in a mode that trusts the 'alg' header from the token itself, allowing an RS256-signed-token verifier to be downgraded to HS256 and validated using the public key as an HMAC secret.
theoretical_attack_kill_chain: Attacker obtains the application's public RSA key from a public JWKS endpoint (standard, non-sensitive exposure)
Attacker crafts a placeholder JWT with header alg changed from RS256 to HS256
Attacker signs the placeholder token using the public key string as the HMAC secret
Attacker submits the forged token to an authenticated endpoint to test whether the server's verification logic accepts the downgraded algorithm
synthetic_server_logs: [app-log] WARN: JWT verified with algorithm HS256 using key material originally provisioned for RS256 — algorithm mismatch flagged
[app-log] ERROR: Privilege-elevated route accessed with token lacking expected issuer claim validation
detection_logic_for_ai: Compare the 'alg' field declared in JWT headers against the application's expected fixed algorithm at verification time, rejecting any mismatch; alert when a token verified via HS256 uses key material known to be an RSA public key; flag auth success events immediately following a prior 401 from the same IP using a structurally different token header.
secure_code_remediation:
import jwt
# Pin the expected algorithm explicitly; never trust the token's own 'alg' header
decoded = jwt.decode(token, public_key, algorithms=['RS256'], audience='api.example.com')

vulnerable_architecture: A document-download endpoint builds a filesystem path by concatenating a 'filename' query parameter with a base directory, without normalizing or restricting the resulting path to the intended folder.
theoretical_attack_kill_chain: Attacker requests a legitimate file to confirm the endpoint's base behavior: /download?file=report_q1.pdf
Attacker submits a relative-path placeholder: /download?file=../../../../etc/placeholder_test.txt
Attacker observes the server returns content outside the intended documents directory
Attacker iterates traversal depth and URL-encodes slashes to test filter bypass resilience
synthetic_server_logs: [app-log] WARN: Resolved file path escaped base directory /var/app/documents — resolved to /etc/placeholder_test.txt
detection_logic_for_ai: Flag filename/path parameters containing '../', URL-encoded traversal sequences (%2e%2e%2f), or absolute path indicators; validate that resolved canonical paths remain within the intended base directory at request time; alert on repeated requests to the same endpoint with varying traversal depth from one source.

vulnerable_architecture: A banking-style fund-transfer form processes POST requests based solely on an authenticated session cookie, with no anti-CSRF token, no SameSite cookie attribute, and no origin/referer validation.
theoretical_attack_kill_chain: Attacker identifies the transfer endpoint accepts simple POST requests with only amount and destination_account parameters
Attacker hosts a placeholder HTML page containing an auto-submitting form targeting the transfer endpoint with test parameter values
Victim, while authenticated to the target site in another tab, visits the attacker's placeholder page
Victim's browser automatically submits the forged request, including the victim's valid session cookie, to the transfer endpoint
synthetic_server_logs: [app-log] WARN: POST to /transfer accepted with cross-origin Referer (attacker-test.example) and no CSRF token present
[app-log] INFO: Transfer request processed: amount=1.00 destination=TEST-ACCT-0000 — flagged post-hoc by fraud review
detection_logic_for_ai: Flag state-changing POST/PUT/DELETE requests lacking a valid anti-CSRF token even when the session cookie is valid; alert when Origin or Referer headers indicate a cross-origin source for sensitive form submissions; treat absence of SameSite=Strict/Lax cookie attributes on session cookies as a contributing architectural risk factor.
